repos.title: SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs
repos.paper_summary:
SurveyGraph is a survey-generation pipeline built around a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph (MEKG) with 21 typed relations among papers, including extends, improves, and applies. The MEKG drives core-paper selection, hybrid outline generation, graph-aware retrieval, and section-level write-evaluate-refine synthesis. A four-layer inference engine creates the relations, and an evidence gate with AUC=0.75 filters semantic edges.

Across eight archived runs, graph-aware retrieval raises core-paper recall from 0.216 to 0.373 over flat lexical retrieval (sign test p=0.004). In a seven-method equal-budget benchmark, MEKG-anchored fusion has higher relation density than flat lexical retrieval at similar recall. Two annotators labeled 108 stratified edges (binary support $\kappa=0.64$), and 68.5% were supported-or-partial after adjudication, with extends lowest at 52.8%. Citation audits over 160 generated sentences found 80.6% anchored-or-partial. A SurveyBench collection-stage probe on four topics reached 0.521 mean reference coverage with an eight-paper budget.

Limitations: the human study covers three relation types from one domain cluster. The MVSS and StructSurvey comparisons are not same-backend reruns. The SurveyBench probes do not test outlining or writing.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Flat retrieval in survey generation misses how methods evolve, so SurveyGraph builds a typed method graph to recover that structure.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work groups survey generators, benchmarks and graph tools, and differs by using one method-entity graph across the full pipeline.

digest_headlines.heading: The SurveyGraph Framework
digest_headlines.headline: The framework builds a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph and reuses it for outlining, retrieval and narrative synthesis.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation Framework
digest_headlines.headline: Evaluation separates graph-native diagnostics, retrieval benchmarks, grounding audits and benchmark alignment into distinct levels.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Graph-aware retrieval raises core-paper recall from 0.216 to 0.373 across eight runs, with p=0.004.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion claims an auditable typed structure layer, while SurveyBench results remain collection-stage diagnostics.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: SurveyBench results are collection-stage probes, and edge validation rests on 108 edges from one domain cluster.

digest_headlines.heading: Ethical Considerations
digest_headlines.headline: Ethical risk is mainly hallucinated citations, and claims were checked against archived artifacts before inclusion.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists artifacts, reproducibility audits, Qwen generation diagnostics, the SurveyBench probe, the evidence-gate threshold analysis and comparison boundaries.

repos.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
repos.paper_summary:
3DCodeVerse is an ecosystem for 3D coding agents with three parts: 3DCodeVerse-2M, a dataset of 2.03 M standalone executable 3D programs with their assets and verification records; a multi-agent harness; and open-model baselines. Programs come from public sources, converted representations (such as DeepCAD sequences translated to CadQuery), and harness-generated code. The harness splits a request into a directed acyclic graph of coding and assembly tasks, executes the output, checks geometry (bounding boxes, contacts, collisions), and has a VLM judge score renders against rubric criteria. Feedback drives repeated revisions without human input.

On 100 text-to-3D object prompts, human evaluators preferred the harness over each model's native harness in 69% to 89% of comparisons. Against Claude Design, both using Claude Opus 5.5, the harness won 90% of human comparisons (Judge Score 88 vs. 37). Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B raised the 3DCodeBench execution rate from 0.0% to 84.9%; Qwen3.8-27B rose from 51.9% to 92.9% with SFT and DPO.

Limitations: the object, scene, and graphics comparisons use 100, 50, and 50 prompts; rubric scores come from a VLM judge; and the fine-tuning results use one decoding seed.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: 3DCodeVerse combines a curated executable 3D code dataset with a harness that verifies and revises generated programs.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior 3D code work covers datasets, benchmarks and feedback harnesses, but these remain fragmented across tasks and environments.

digest_headlines.heading: 3DCodeVerse-2M: A large-scale 3D coding dataset
digest_headlines.headline: 3DCodeVerse-2M packages standalone executable 3D programs with assets, captions and separate verification records.

digest_headlines.heading: 3DCodeVerse Harness: A Data Engine for 3D Coding
digest_headlines.headline: The harness uses a multi-agent graph with execution, spatial and visual feedback to revise programs without human input.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Harness outputs win most human comparisons, reaching 90% against Claude Design, and fine-tuning raises execution rates.

digest_headlines.heading: Applications of 3D coding
digest_headlines.headline: Code renders pass a door-and-handle geometry check in 12/12 outputs, versus 7/36 for a frozen video world-action model.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The authors plan to release datasets, harness, models and training recipes after reporting open-model and harness results.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix details harness runtimes, planning, judge scoring, a recorded run, articulation checks and a video-model comparison.

repos.title: LoongSage: A Production-Grade, High-Efficiency Agentic RL Framework for Frontier LLMs with Validated Recipes
repos.paper_summary:
LoongSage is an agent-native reinforcement learning framework for LLM post-training, built on Megatron for training and SGLang for inference, with about 14K lines of core code. Its AgentFlow layer serves agents through a Chat Completions interface and stores trajectories at the token level (Token-In, Token-Out), so sampled and trained sequences match. Black-box agents with context compaction or subagents are stored as a segment tree, and only mainline segments are trained. Three sliding-window policies bound staleness in fully asynchronous mode: no-window, window-gated (staleness at most S steps), and windowed-fifo (collection limited to one batch). TransferMesh selects a weight-transfer transport per receiver topology, such as CUDA IPC for colocated GPUs or NCCL for distributed nodes. A Teacher Manager supports multi-teacher on-policy distillation with sampled-token, top-K, full-vocabulary, and JSD estimators.

The evidence is four complete training runs, reported as steady task-reward improvement, a controlled train–inference gap, and reduced idle time. The paper does not provide a theorem. Its limitations include multi-agent credit assignment, which is left as non-trainable placeholders, and support for proprietary agent APIs, which is still under development.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Existing RL frameworks add overhead for agentic training, so the paper proposes LoongSage, built on Megatron and SGLang.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work argues that existing RL frameworks lack explicit support for agentic trajectories, resource sharing, and rollout–optimization boundaries.

digest_headlines.heading: The LoongSage Framework
digest_headlines.headline: The architecture uses one controller over Ray actors, token-level internal interfaces, and seven planes, with three of four placement combinations supported.

digest_headlines.heading: Key Features
digest_headlines.headline: AgentFlow stores white-box and black-box agent trajectories as token arrays and segment trees, and three sliding-window policies bound asynchronous staleness.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Four training runs show rising rewards with bounded train–inference gaps, and asynchronous execution gives a 1.35× speedup.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion lists six contributions and plans to add Proximal Policy Optimization, Supervised Fine-Tuning, and Low-Rank Adaptation.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists author names and operational notes on hard failures, silent corruptions, and current implementation boundaries.

repos.title: One Token Is Enough: Fingerprinting and Verifying Large Language Models from Single-Token Output Distributions
repos.paper_summary: The paper proposes a black-box fingerprint for LLMs: the empirical distribution of single-token answers to trivial prompts such as "name a random number between 1 and 100," sampled at temperature 1.0 in four languages with reasoning disabled and a 16-token cap. Across 165 models served through OpenRouter, the median cell entropy is 1.00 bit. The median Jensen–Shannon divergence between split halves of one model is 0.075, versus 0.489 between different models. Leave-one-out nearest-neighbour classification assigns a model to its documented family with 59.5% accuracy, against an 18.4% chance rate. A verification test gives a 7.3% equal error rate with all 40 cells and 10.6% with eight cells; a 16-cell audit uses 240 single-token queries. Verifying against a reference from a different provider gives AUC 0.880, versus 0.971 for the same provider. Limitations: fingerprints drift with model updates, multi-month drift was not measured, paraphrase invariance is left to future work, the census covers one aggregator, and endpoints with hidden reasoning were excluded. One endpoint marketed as proprietary lies at distance 0.141 from an open-weight Qwen model.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Served LLMs often differ from advertised models, so clients need a cheap, text-only identity check.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior attribution work needs long outputs, logits, or owner cooperation; this study uses one-token answers.

digest_headlines.heading: Threat Model
digest_headlines.headline: The verifier sees only text and a trusted reference, facing adversaries that substitute, filter, or emulate.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: Each model is fingerprinted by answer distributions over ten tasks in four languages, compared with Jensen–Shannon divergence.

digest_headlines.heading: Experimental Setup
digest_headlines.headline: The census covers 165 models from 342 catalog entries, 326,047 responses, and a total cost of USD 34.44.

digest_headlines.heading: Results
digest_headlines.headline: Fingerprints separate models and recover lineage at 59.5% accuracy against 18.4% chance, with 7.3% equal error rate verification.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Cross-provider shifts stay below impostor distances, and no response-caching signature appears in the census.

digest_headlines.heading: Ethics and Responsible Disclosure
digest_headlines.headline: Anomalies are framed as statistical deviations with benign explanations, and no security exploit is involved.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Single-token audits are a near-zero-cost check, with longitudinal drift and watermark-aware variants left to future work.

repos.title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
repos.paper_summary: The paper presents Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO), an RL training method for large language models that stabilizes asynchronous updates by replacing group-wise sampling with single-rollout updates. SAO computes the importance ratio $r_t(\theta) = \exp(\log\pi_\theta(a_t|s_t) - \log\pi_{\text{rollout}}(a_t|s_t))$ directly from rollout log-probabilities, eliminating the need to track historical policy checkpoints. It applies a double-sided token-level clipping function that masks gradients for tokens outside a defined interval, preventing instability from extreme policy divergence. To reduce variance in single-rollout advantage estimation, SAO trains a value model with frozen attention layers and performs two critic updates per policy update. For multi-turn agent trajectories, it uses a skip-observation GAE estimator that calculates advantages across action-to-action boundaries, bypassing environment feedback tokens. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, SAO achieves 97.3% accuracy on AIME2025 and 29.8% on SWE-Bench Verified, outperforming GRPO variants that collapse after approximately 160 steps. The authors note that results are specific to large-scale agentic tasks and may not transfer to smaller models or non-agentic settings.

repos.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
repos.paper_summary: Hy-Nomas is an 8B-parameter video world model that generates interactive video from free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple turns. It is built on HunyuanVideo 1.5 and generates variable-length segments conditioned on the current input and cached history. Its main design choice is action-aware causal attention: structured captions describe persistent scene and subject context that stays visible to later segments, while timestamped action instructions are limited to their own time window. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer converts user requests and interaction history into structured conditions for each next segment. Training follows a multi-stage curriculum (causal generation, text interaction, camera control, training on model-generated histories), then diffusion distillation. Human evaluation is reported as favoring Hy-Nomas over existing world models, but the text provided does not include the scores. The paper notes that temporal causality does not establish physical causality, that robotics adaptation is shown only as an initial LoRA demonstration, and that retrieving past views does not update off-screen state, such as a clock that should keep running. Weights, code, and benchmarks are released.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hy-Nomas is an 8B interactive world model that follows free-form text and camera commands across multiple turns.

digest_headlines.heading: Data
digest_headlines.headline: Training videos are filtered, deduplicated, and annotated with camera trajectories and structured captions.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Architecture
digest_headlines.headline: Action-aware causal attention limits each action to its own time window, and camera tokens condition each segment.

digest_headlines.heading: Training Infrastructure
digest_headlines.headline: Sequence parallelism, compute-balanced packing and masked attention kernels support training on sequences up to 360K tokens.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Training
digest_headlines.headline: Training proceeds through causal, interaction and context curricula, then distillation from 100 to 4 steps per segment.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Inference
digest_headlines.headline: A vision-language Prompt Enhancer turns user requests into segment captions, and inference is optimized for a single device.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Human raters prefer Hy-Nomas over three interactive world models on most tasks, but Genie 3 leads on spatial memory.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Hy-Nomas is placed among video-based world models that add text and camera control to diffusion video generators.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion and Future Directions
digest_headlines.headline: Discussion names open challenges: response latency, action-grounded robotics, retrieval-based memory, and detailed caption quality.

digest_headlines.heading: Contributors
digest_headlines.headline: Contributors section lists core contributors, contributors, acknowledgments and leadership acknowledgments.

repos.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
repos.paper_summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a training algorithm that aligns language models with human preferences using a binary cross-entropy loss, eliminating the need for reinforcement learning. DPO derives this objective by reparameterizing the reward function in standard RLHF as $\hat{r}(x,y) = \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y|x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y|x)}$, where $\pi_\theta$ is the policy being trained and $\pi_{\text{ref}}$ is a fixed reference model. This substitution allows the optimal policy to be extracted in closed form from the Bradley-Terry preference model. The paper proves that under mild assumptions, this reparameterization preserves the full class of representable reward functions without loss of generality. Experiments on IMDb sentiment generation, Reddit TL;DR summarization, and Anthropic dialogue tasks show DPO matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF performance. In sentiment control, DPO achieves higher expected reward at equivalent KL-divergence levels than PPO. For summarization and dialogue, GPT-4 evaluations indicate DPO win rates are comparable to or better than PPO baselines. Limitations include evaluation reliance on GPT-4 judgments and untested scaling beyond 6B parameter models.

repos.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
repos.paper_summary: InteractiveWorld is a simulator built on Isaac Sim for closed-loop interaction between an egocentric MLLM assistant and a human. InteractiveBench is a set of 120 multi-turn tasks in six categories: Guidance, Planning, Accessibility, Decision, Prevention, and Finding. The human is an MLLM agent (Gemini 3.1 Pro in the main experiments) that follows the assistant's guidance and issues one of 36 action primitives. A kinematically driven SMPL+H body performs navigation and manipulation. Success is checked automatically from final object states. Twelve models were evaluated as the assistant. Claude Fable 5.1 passes 41.7% of tasks, and all other models reach at most 33.3%. The best models reach 20.0% on Guidance and 25.0% on Planning, compared with 85.0% on Decision for the best model. With the same human agent, an oracle assistant passes all tasks. Perception and memory errors account for 70.4%–85.7% of first errors across models. The human is simulated by an MLLM rather than real people, and visual input per turn is capped at 32 frames.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Static video benchmarks cannot test whether interactive assistants help people, so the paper proposes a closed-loop simulated environment and benchmark.

digest_headlines.heading: InteractiveWorld
digest_headlines.headline: InteractiveWorld models a human who follows assistant guidance, using kinematic body control, collision checks and 36 action primitives.

digest_headlines.heading: InteractiveBench
digest_headlines.headline: InteractiveBench has 120 human-reviewed tasks in six categories, scored by final simulator object states rather than answer matching.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: The strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, passes 41.7% of tasks, and the best models reach only 20.0% on Guidance and 25.0% on Planning.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: InteractiveWorld and InteractiveBench provide a verifiable foundation for developing and evaluating interactive MLLM assistants.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers related work, simulator implementation, benchmark construction and metrics, extra analyses, human-executor validation and future work.

repos.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
repos.paper_summary: The paper presents Megatron-LM, a method for training multi-billion parameter transformer language models using intra-layer model parallelism in PyTorch. The approach partitions the self-attention and MLP blocks across GPUs by splitting weight matrices column-wise for the first linear layer and row-wise for the second, requiring only two all-reduce operations per forward pass. This design avoids custom compilers and is orthogonal to pipeline parallelism. On 512 NVIDIA V100 GPUs, an 8.3 billion parameter GPT-2 model sustains 15.1 PetaFLOPs with 76% scaling efficiency relative to a single-GPU baseline. The same architecture trains a 3.9 billion parameter BERT variant, where rearranging layer normalization before residual connections prevents degradation observed in standard BERT at larger scales. The 8.3B GPT-2 model achieves a WikiText103 perplexity of 10.8 and LAMBADA accuracy of 66.5%, while the 3.9B BERT model reaches 90.9% accuracy on RACE. Limitations include the requirement for high-bandwidth interconnects like NVLink or InfiniBand, and the fact that the BERT results are reported on development sets for most tasks except RACE.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Megatron-LM trains transformers up to 8.3 billion parameters with intra-layer model parallelism, reaching 76% scaling efficiency on 512 GPUs.

digest_headlines.heading: Background and Challenges
digest_headlines.headline: Existing model parallel methods need custom compilers or pipeline changes, so the authors modify only a PyTorch transformer.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Parallel Transformers
digest_headlines.headline: The MLP and attention blocks are split across GPUs so each transformer layer needs only four all-reduce operations.

digest_headlines.heading: Setup
digest_headlines.headline: GPT-2 and BERT models train on an aggregated 174 GB deduplicated corpus with fixed optimizer and learning-rate schedules.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Model parallel scaling reaches 77% of linear scaling at 8.3 billion parameters, and GPT-2 and BERT results set new SOTA marks.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion and Future Work
digest_headlines.headline: The authors conclude that intra-layer parallelism scales to 8.3 billion parameters and suggest hybrid parallelism for larger models.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists BERT finetuning hyperparameters, hybrid parallelism and random number details, text samples, evaluation methodology, and strong scaling results.

repos.title: Monocular Identity-Conditioned Facial Reflectance Reconstruction
repos.paper_summary: ID2Reflectance is a framework for monocular facial reflectance reconstruction that estimates diffuse albedo, specular albedo, roughness, and surface normal maps from a single in-the-wild image. The method learns a facial prior in image space rather than UV space to reduce dependency on limited light-stage data. It trains a VQGAN with multi-domain codebooks, aligning RGB and reflectance domains by jointly training on FFHQ and 135 captured subjects. An identity-conditioned swapper module, trained on VGGFace2HQ using AdaIN, injects identity features from the target image into the pre-trained decoder. At inference, the system synthesizes three-view reflectance images and stitches them into UV-space maps. On a test set of 20 subjects, ID2Reflectance achieves a PSNR of 28.47 dB for diffuse albedo, outperforming TRUST (21.63 dB) and ID2Albedo (23.72 dB). Identity similarity reaches 0.735 compared to 0.532 for ID2Albedo. The total inference time is 3.8 seconds per face on an A6000 GPU. The paper notes that reconstructed PBR maps may not be physically plausible due to the lack of ground-truth supervision.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Reflectance models trained on few light-stage captures generalize poorly, so the method learns the reflectance prior in image space from abundant RGB faces.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior facial reflectance methods depend on light-stage data and their data is unreleased, while face swapping methods target only the RGB domain.

digest_headlines.heading: Methodology
digest_headlines.headline: Two-stage codebook training aligns reflectance with RGB, so identity swapping learned on RGB transfers to reflectance maps.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Trained on 115 captured subjects, the method gives identity-preserved reflectance on Digital Emily and in-the-wild faces in 3.8 seconds/face.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusions and Discussions
digest_headlines.headline: The paper concludes that limited captured data yields a reliable reflectance prior and notes the method could be misused.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers the light stage rig, public datasets, codebook and swapper details, UV stitching, a fairness benchmark, and further qualitative results.
